summary: As our downtown communities grow and become more dense with residents, jobs, and visitors, it is increasingly important that we are making the most of our existing parks and public spaces. Downtown already has a parkland provision 67% below the City-wide average, and the residential population is projected to more than double by 2041. The Council-approved Downtown Parks and Public Realm Plan includes four objectives to support liveable and healthy downtown communities: acquire and expand; improve; share; and connect. Victoria Memorial Square Park is a heavily-used public park near the intersection of Wellington Street West and Bathurst Street, which has at its centre the earliest known cemetery associated with Fort York and the Town of York. At least 400 people were buried there before the cemetery was closed in 1863. In the 2000s, as a new residential neighbourhood grew up around it, the local community and the City of Toronto undertook a major revitalization to rehabilitate the park and celebrate its past. Due to the high volume of activity in the park today, it requires intensive ongoing maintenance by City staff to keep up with wear and tear. Wellington Street West is a public street that forms the northern limit of Victoria Memorial Square and for most of this boundary, the pavement is unusually wide. The extra pavement does not extend to the Bathurst Street intersection…
decided: The Toronto and East York Community Council: 1. Requested the Director, Public Realm Section, Transportation Services, to report back to the Toronto and East York Community Council on: a. the temporary closure, to vehicular traffic, of the southerly curb lane of Wellington Street West, west of Portland Street and adjacent to Victoria Memorial Square Park for near-term public realm and pedestrian improvements; and b. the permanent closure of the southerly curb lane of Wellington Street West, west of Portland Street, for the purpose of enlarging Victoria Memorial Square Park.
